finding: CH-independence treatment does not prove \(\mathsf{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC})\Rightarrow\mathsf{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC}+\neg\mathrm{CH})\): the sketch uses the countable-transitive-model presentation that the adjacent Warning (9107) says does not suffice, and the nonderivability step invokes soundness over two structures never produced, so the theorem statement (9066) overclaims.
required_fix: Rewrite per the book's own Warning: either present relative consistency with honest cited status or give the correct syntactic route (forcing over finite fragments / ctm with the inaccessibility caveat), deleting the two-structures soundness justification.
acceptance: Revised passage claims only what its displayed argument or citation actually establishes, and the nonderivability justification is syntactic with no appeal to unexhibited structures.

finding: Coding inconsistency: the text asserts iterated Cantor pairing is not the coding used for bounded verification while the fixed machine numbering is built from exactly that pairing, so \(\mathsf{Comp}(e,x,s)\) lacks the bounded extraction from \(e\) it needs (the beta-function is applied only to histories), and the gap propagates to the \(\Sigma^0_1\) status of \(\mathsf{Prov}_T\).
required_fix: Adopt a single coding with a proved bounded-extraction lemma covering machine codes as well as histories, and re-derive the \(\Sigma^0_1\) form of \(\mathsf{Comp}\) and \(\mathsf{Prov}_T\) from it.
acceptance: One coding is used consistently, the bounded-extraction lemma is a labeled proved result, and the \(\Sigma^0_1\) claims for \(\mathsf{Comp}\) and \(\mathsf{Prov}_T\) cite it with no contradictory prose remaining.

finding: Rosser sketch uses the object symbol \(\leq\), never defined or registered anywhere (only \(<\) at 6924), and silently uses two unstated Q-lemmas (bounded-case enumeration and the dichotomy \(y\leq\bar n\lor\bar n\leq y\)) that carry the proof's only nontrivial content.
required_fix: Define and register object \(\leq\) (or eliminate it in favor of \(<\)) and state and prove or cite both Q-lemmas as labeled results before the sketch uses them.
acceptance: \(\leq\) has a registered definition and both Q-lemmas exist as labeled statused results that the Rosser argument references explicitly.

finding: The jump is defined via halting although the numbering makes \(\varphi_e(e)\) undefined on halt-without-valid-output, mismatching \(K\), and the jump theorem is asserted in unlabeled prose without proof or citation while load-bearing for hierarchy strictness (7180--7189).
required_fix: Align the halting predicate with the numbering's convergence notion (or adjust the numbering) and promote the jump theorem to a labeled result with status and proof or citation.
acceptance: \(K\) and the jump use one convergence notion consistent with the numbering, and the jump theorem is a labeled statused result referenced by the strictness argument.

finding: The enumeration theorem for the program numbering (every partial computable function occurs in it) is asserted in unlabeled prose without proof while load-bearing for Rice, the recursion theorem, and Post.
required_fix: State the enumeration theorem as a labeled result with a proof (or precise citation) tied to the constructed numbering.
acceptance: A labeled statused enumeration theorem exists and is referenced at Rice, the recursion theorem, and Post.

finding: The closure-class definition of the arithmetical hierarchy (with bounded-quantifier closure) is never proved equivalent to the prefix-normal-form characterization; the required bounded-collection lemma is missing.
required_fix: State and prove the bounded-collection lemma and derive the closure-class/prenex equivalence as a labeled theorem.
acceptance: The equivalence is a labeled result with complete proof and downstream hierarchy results reference it.

finding: Prenex normal form theorem rests on an unstated and unproved first-order NNF existence theorem, unproved existence of rectified alpha-variants, and an unstated rectification-preservation invariant; the propositional NNF theorem (1899) does not transfer.
required_fix: Prove first-order NNF existence and rectified-variant existence as labeled lemmas, state the preservation invariant, and run the prenex induction on them.
acceptance: The prenex proof cites only proved first-order lemmas and makes no appeal to the propositional NNF theorem.

finding: Skolemization equisatisfiability is labeled complete but is a sketch: no induction hypothesis is formulated, the unregistered term quantifier game is used (no game semantics exists in the book), and AC is over-assumed for the choice-free direction.
required_fix: Write the induction with an explicit hypothesis and cases, remove or define the game terminology, and separate the AC-using direction from the choice-free one.
acceptance: The proof displays its induction hypothesis and cases, AC appears only in the direction that needs it, and no unregistered terminology remains.

finding: The Henkin--Lindenbaum maximality step silently reuses the omega-recursion argument of the propositional Lindenbaum lemma where a transfinite recursion with limit stages and a chain argument is needed (the nearby witness stage does invoke transfinite recursion properly).
required_fix: Redo the maximality step by transfinite recursion with explicit successor and limit stages and the union/chain argument.
acceptance: The maximality construction displays successor and limit cases and the chain argument, with no out-of-scope appeal to the propositional lemma.

finding: The substitution/alpha lemma applies structural induction to \(\psi[z/y]\), which is not a subformula of the original formula, so the induction principle invoked does not apply.
required_fix: Recast as strong induction on formula complexity via the substitution-complexity lemma, the fix the book itself uses at 2951--2958 and 3195--3199.
acceptance: The induction is on complexity, cites the substitution-complexity lemma, and every case reduces to strictly lower complexity.

finding: The CNF half of the propositional normal-form theorem is procedural with no induction or termination argument and fails degenerate cases (valid or variable-free formulas) against the book's rigid CNF definition; the DNF half is exemplary.
required_fix: Give the CNF half a genuine induction (or dualize the DNF argument) with the degenerate cases handled explicitly.
acceptance: The CNF proof is a complete induction whose output satisfies the book's CNF definition on all inputs including degenerate ones.

finding: The cut-elimination sketch invokes a mix/multicut rule that is never displayed anywhere, states the termination measure for Cut rather than mix, and two corollaries with full proof environments rest on the sketch, violating the release checklist's own rule (14346).
required_fix: Display and label the mix rule, restate the measure for the rule actually eliminated, and either complete the induction or downgrade the corollaries' status to match the sketch.
acceptance: The mix rule is displayed and labeled, the measure matches it, and no complete-proof result depends on a sketch.

finding: ND repetition is permitted in prose but is not among the twelve displayed rules, and vacuous discharge is never licensed although the completeness proof needs it; the first-order analogue (3804--3806) handles both explicitly.
required_fix: Add repetition to the displayed rule inventory (or derive it) and license vacuous discharge explicitly, matching the first-order treatment.
acceptance: Every rule and discharge convention used by the propositional completeness proof appears in the displayed rule inventory.

finding: LK completeness is stated only for single-formula succedents, strictly weaker than LK soundness for arbitrary sequents, and the book never closes the loop for arbitrary sequents.
required_fix: State and prove LK completeness for arbitrary sequents, or scope both metatheorems to the same sequent class with an explicit remark.
acceptance: Soundness and completeness are paired over the same class of sequents or an explicit labeled remark records the asymmetry.

finding: Model completeness of DLO is defined by quantification over all embeddings but the proof treats only substructure inclusions; the reduction step is missing.
required_fix: Add the reduction from arbitrary embeddings to substructure inclusions or restate the definition to match the proof.
acceptance: The proof covers exactly the quantifier range of the definition.

finding: The back-and-forth corollary uses an extends-the-original-map clause that is available from the proof but absent from the theorem statement, which concludes only isomorphism.
required_fix: Add the extension clause to the theorem statement.
acceptance: The corollary cites only clauses present in the theorem statement.

finding: Mixed-status theorem thm:infinite-cardinal-finite-coding: one label covers clauses cited to Jech, a clause unlocatable in the cited source, and a clause proved inline, against the status policy at 313--319.
required_fix: Split into separately labeled results with per-clause status and locate or reprove the unlocatable clause.
acceptance: Each clause carries exactly one status and every cited clause is locatable in its source.

finding: The associativity-of-concatenation proof is a plan rather than a proof: the announced induction is not carried out.
required_fix: Write the induction on string length in full.
acceptance: The proof displays base case and inductive step with the induction variable identified.

finding: The complexity-recursion example precedes the unique-readability theorem it depends on.
required_fix: Reorder so unique readability precedes the example, or add an explicit forward-dependency remark.
acceptance: No example depends on a later result without an explicit forward reference.

finding: The path characterization of the transitive closure \(R^*\) is used without proof.
required_fix: State and prove the path characterization as a labeled lemma or mark its status honestly.
acceptance: The characterization is a labeled result with status and proof or citation.

finding: The controlled-prose translation table and its commentary on only and unless contain translation errors.
required_fix: Correct the offending table rows and the accompanying only/unless commentary.
acceptance: Every table row and commentary claim is semantically correct under the book's registered semantics.

finding: The LK soundness wording slides between valid and satisfied.
required_fix: Rewrite the soundness argument keeping the two registered notions distinct throughout.
acceptance: Each occurrence of valid and satisfied matches its registered definition.

finding: Davis--Putnam elimination is unattributed and stated for finite clause sets only, with no remark relating the finite restriction to compactness.
required_fix: Add the primary-source attribution and an explicit finiteness/compactness scope remark.
acceptance: The passage carries a citation and a scope remark delimiting the finite case.

finding: Conservativity of definitional extensions is asserted in an example without proof although Beth definability later leans on it.
required_fix: State conservativity of definitional extensions as a labeled result with proof or citation.
acceptance: A labeled statused conservativity result exists and is referenced where used.

finding: The LK universal-quantifier-right soundness case is hand-waved.
required_fix: Write the case in full with the eigenvariable condition doing explicit semantic work.

finding: The compactness theorem statement is garbled (a dangling equivalently-clause mixes the model form with the consequence form) and the proof closes the loop redundantly.

finding: Broken forward promise: the front matter promises countable-language versions of the completeness theorems, but no countable or choice-free completeness theorem exists anywhere, and the AC hypothesis on completeness (4127) is thereby over-stated for the countable case.

finding: The type-space compactness proof omits the complete-type/Lindenbaum step while presented as complete.

acceptance: Every step of the argument is displayed or the result carries sketch status.

finding: The saturation-implies-homogeneity proof omits its compactness appeal while presented as complete.
required_fix: Supply the compactness appeal explicitly or downgrade the result's status.
acceptance: The compactness use is displayed and cited or the result carries sketch status.

finding: The DLO \(\aleph_0\)-categoricity proof suppresses the four interval cases, which are supplied only by the exercise solution at 13692 -- the appendix doing the theorem's work.

finding: The injectivity step in the second-order categoricity proof is hand-waved.
required_fix: Write the injectivity argument in full.
acceptance: The injectivity argument is displayed with its induction or case analysis.

finding: \(\mathrm{PA}_2\) is used but never defined.
required_fix: Define \(\mathrm{PA}_2\) (language, axioms, semantics) before first use in the migrated part.
acceptance: The definition precedes every use of the symbol.

finding: Failure of downward L\"owenheim--Skolem for full second-order semantics is justified by an undisplayed, unproved, uncited categoricity of the second-order reals.
required_fix: State the second-order categoricity of the reals as a labeled result with status and citation, and cite it in the justification.
acceptance: The justification cites a labeled statused result.

finding: The ordinal trichotomy proof idea (foundation applied to the symmetric difference) is not a recognizable argument.

acceptance: The proof idea matches a correct standard proof outline.

finding: The definition of partial computable is malformed by a double iff.

finding: Nonprincipal-ultrafilter existence is unlabeled prose whose induction is not carried out.
required_fix: Promote to a labeled result and carry out the chain/Zorn argument or cite it.
acceptance: A labeled statused result exists whose proof is complete or cited.

finding: Finite-matrix tableau completeness wears a proof environment over a sketch (the induction is asserted, not performed) and uses the term saturated, never defined anywhere in the book.
required_fix: Define saturation for the tableau system and either perform the induction or downgrade the result to sketch status.

finding: The DPLL correctness proof is one sentence over a two-specification claim, violating the book's own template at 11791 and style rule 12354.
required_fix: Supply the two-part correctness argument or downgrade to sketch status under the migration's compile-enforced status scheme.

finding: Common knowledge dangles: \(C_G\) receives language and semantics but no axioms or induction rule anywhere, the non-compactness/weak-completeness caveat stated for LTL (11090) is omitted for \(C_G\), and an exercise then uses it.

finding: The G\"odel--Gentzen translation recursion is not literally well-defined: whether \(\bot\) counts as atomic (priority of the \(\bot\)-clause versus the double-negation clause for atoms) is unstated.

finding: The prime-theory description is ambiguous between \(\vdash A\lor B\) and \(T\vdash A\lor B\).

acceptance: The definition determines a unique class of theories.

finding: The rule sheet declares the equality rules part of the complete active first-order sequent calculus while the cut-elimination sketch never treats equality rules, so two passages refer to different calculi under one name; the sheet's symmetry-derivability claim is correct but silently requires cut.

acceptance: Every calculus name refers to one rule inventory and every metatheorem names the calculus it is proved for.

finding: The book's three-term status policy is scoped to Part IV onward by the convention at 5007, leaving 56 of 66 numbered results in Parts I--III silently presented as complete proofs with no status labels.
required_fix: Extend the status convention book-wide and label every Part I--III result, via the new tree's compile-enforced status keys.
acceptance: 100 percent status coverage on numbered results in Parts I--III.

finding: Notation collision against the front-matter policy (239--241): \(|\cdot|\) denotes both cardinality (550) and structure domain (3028), yielding nested-bars expressions at 4317 and 4386.

finding: Notation collision: \(\equiv\) carries four roles (metalinguistic sign, propositional equivalence, first-order equivalence, elementary equivalence -- the last registered mid-theorem at 4371).
required_fix: Ratify and enforce the ruling: \(\equiv\) is elementary equivalence only, formula equivalence is \(\Leftrightarrow\), and the definitional sign is \(:\equiv\).
acceptance: Each of the three glyphs maps to exactly one registered role book-wide.

finding: Parameter notation \(\varphi(\bar x)\) lacks the side condition \(\mathrm{FV}(\varphi)\subseteq\{\bar x\}\) and conflicts with the variable-indexing convention at 4324.
required_fix: State the side condition in the notation's registration and reconcile it with the variable indexing.
acceptance: The registered entry carries the side condition and no conflicting use remains.

finding: The Ultrafilter Lemma, an existence theorem, is housed in a definition environment (hence unlabeled and unsourced) and contains an uncited independence claim (strictly weaker than AC over ZF).
required_fix: Rehouse as a labeled theorem with status and add the Halpern--L\'evy citation.
acceptance: The lemma is a labeled statused theorem with the independence claim cited.

finding: Results are cited at whole-chapter level because the intended targets are unlabeled examples.
required_fix: Label the target results and repoint the citations at result level.
acceptance: No chapter-level citation stands in for a result-level one.

finding: Status coverage collapses after Parts IV--VI: 26 of 77 theorem/lemma/corollary environments in the segment carry no status (all of Part VII zero, Part VIII two).
required_fix: Apply the compile-enforced status keys of the new tree to every result in the segment.
acceptance: 100 percent status coverage on results in Parts IV--IX.

finding: Three inconsistent status mechanisms are in use (Status line with proofplan environment, bare paragraph Proof sketch, paragraph Cited theorem), split by page range -- the same defect the production audit records as two sketch mechanisms (proofplan 10 times before 7710, paragraph 20 times after).
required_fix: Adopt exactly one compile-enforced status mechanism book-wide.
acceptance: Exactly one status mechanism appears in the new tree.

finding: The four most important imported results -- the forcing theorem, Gentzen's consistency theorem, and both Henkin completeness theorems -- are unnumbered, unlabeled paragraphs with no TOC or index presence.
required_fix: Promote all four to numbered, labeled, statused theorem environments.
acceptance: All four are numbered results, present in the TOC and index, and citable by label.

finding: Misclassification: results labeled sketch are by the book's own three-way definition cited theorems.
required_fix: Relabel with the correct status.
acceptance: Every status label matches the book's own definition of that status.

finding: Uncountable categoricity of \(\mathrm{ACF}_p\) is packaged as an uncited example (Steinitz).
required_fix: Promote to a labeled statused result with the Steinitz citation.
acceptance: The result is labeled with status and citation.

finding: Name clash: LK denotes two different calculi -- Parts II/III's presentation with primitive negation rules and contexted initial sequents (reproduced by the back-matter rule sheets) versus Part VIII's variant with defined negation and context-free identity -- with no reconciliation, and the cut-elimination sketch is by its own admission incomplete for the former (9258--9260).

acceptance: One canonical LK exists and the variant has its own name and a labeled equivalence theorem.

finding: Analytic derivation appears as a chapter title but is never defined.
required_fix: Define the term at first use or retitle the chapter.
acceptance: Every technical term used in a title is defined or registered.

finding: Status policy is nearly absent in Parts X--XI and the back matter: 3 Status lines in 4,159 lines, with 48 of the book's 60 status labels sitting in lines 5000--7999.
required_fix: Apply the compile-enforced status keys to every result in the segment.
acceptance: 100 percent status coverage on results in Parts X--XI and the back matter.

finding: The modal theorem titled Frame correspondence and completeness contains no correspondence claim -- the book's own warned-against failure mode (12357).
required_fix: Retitle the theorem or add the correspondence statement it advertises.
acceptance: The title asserts exactly what the theorem states.

finding: The IPL completeness sketch omits its inline citation (the controlling sources) where the modal, LTL, and epistemic sketches all cite inline.
required_fix: Add the inline citation.
acceptance: Every sketch relying on external sources cites them inline.

finding: Primary-source rule violated: Glivenko 1929, G\"odel 1933, and Gentzen 1936 are absent from the bibliography (their results cited only to Troelstra volumes) and the many-valued chapter has zero citations (no Kleene at K3, no Priest 1979 at LP), against the book's own rules at 12568 and 14354.
required_fix: Add the primary sources, cite them at point of use, and enforce the no-zero-citation-chapter check as a standing control.
acceptance: The named primaries are present and cited at the results they originate and no chapter has zero citations.

finding: Rule displays violate the book's own naming requirement (12518): the four exponential rules appear as bare unnamed fractions, and the resolution rule's soundness-critical side conditions (renaming apart, mgu) live only in prose.
required_fix: Name and label every rule and display its side conditions as part of the rule, sourced from the calculus registry.
acceptance: Every displayed rule carries a name, a label, and its side conditions.

finding: Three imported theorems live in prose with no status or label: SAT NP-completeness, FOL validity computably enumerable and undecidable (with no citation at all), and refutational completeness.
required_fix: Promote each to a labeled, statused, cited statement.
acceptance: All three are labeled results with status and citation.

finding: Same-glyph collisions within the segment: \(A\) as formula metavariable and monoid carrier in the same chapter, \(v\) as world versus registered valuation, \(u,v,w\) registered as strings but used as worlds, \(M\) as matrix versus structure, and \(V\) and \(D\) carrying three and four roles.
required_fix: Apply the glyph-role rulings and the symbol-registry lint of the new tree.
acceptance: The registry lint reports zero role collisions.

finding: The Kripke forcing relation is typeset with two different macros in the body (10677) and the Exercise Feedback chapter (14071), and the second macro is unregistered.
required_fix: Ratify one registered forcing macro and use it everywhere.
acceptance: Exactly one forcing macro appears in the tree and it is registered.

finding: Release-checklist self-test fails: the book fails four items of its own editorial checklist (undefined saturated, glyph roles, inductions without objects and cases, primary sources) while passing 14339 and 14366--14367.
required_fix: Make the release checklist a mechanically checked phase gate and re-run it at release.
acceptance: The checklist passes mechanically with zero manual waivers.

finding: The five-condition definition template is applied only sporadically in the set-theory chapters (poset filter and genericity, names and extension, semantic forcing), leaving sibling definitions unstructured.

finding: Chapters 10 and 12 contain no exercises while every other chapter in the segment carries them (40 exercises in Parts I--III).

finding: The qualifying-examination chapter poses ten problems but supplies solutions for only five; the final five are listed without solutions.
required_fix: None: qualifying problems are retired from print to verification assets by the format decision.
acceptance: The finding is recorded; no handbook deliverable depends on it.

finding: Compile breaker: amsmath parses the bracketed discharge annotation \({[A]}\) immediately after a matrix opening as the matrix's optional alignment argument, producing an illegal-preamble-token error.

finding: Dead macros (BV, Theory, eqdef, HOL, coNP, CNF, DNF, bracket, paren, id -- the complexity-class macros suggesting planned-never-written content -- plus the later-retired proofplan environment).

finding: Array rows switch inconsistently between the cr primitive and the double-backslash line terminator.

finding: The rule-typesetting macro produces mixed small-caps metrics and overwide multi-premise displays (disjunction elimination, existential elimination).

finding: Two part headings are unlabeled while the other nine are labeled.

finding: The listings package is configured but unused in Parts I--III.

finding: The book has no figures at all in 14,780 lines while tikz and three libraries are loaded: no syntax trees, derivation trees, Kripke diagrams, or hierarchy pictures.

finding: Unused packages (mathrsfs, bm, multirow) and the unused color LogicRed.
